about.text: Paint whose binder is casein dissolved in an alkali, usually lime, or ammonium carbonate or borax; it dries fast to a matt film that becomes water-resistant with time. Used for murals, and by commercial illustrators until the late 1960s.

how.text: Borax casein is the artists' route: pH neutral and longer-lasting than lime casein.

steps.name: mix
steps.note: 1 part casein powder with borax, 1 tablespoon in 8 tablespoons hot water per batch.
In a double boiler; do not exceed it.

steps.name: mix
steps.note: The pigment is worked to a paste with a palette knife, then mixed with the binder.
